subject: Business Models
title: Product-as-a-Service
description: A micro-lesson that makes Product-as-a-Service usable.

hook.text: Michelin sells 'tires-as-a-service' to trucking companies. Pay per mile driven, not per tire purchased.

buildup.text: Product-as-a-service transforms purchases into ongoing services: pay for use, not ownership.

discovery.text: Michelin maintains and replaces tires itself, ensuring optimal performance. It profits when tires last longer.

twist.text: This flips the incentive: manufacturers benefit from durability, not planned obsolescence. Longer life = more profit.

climax.text: Product-as-a-service aligns manufacturer incentives with sustainability. It's profitable and environmentally sound.

punchline.text: Pay per mile, not per tire. When durability profits, sustainability follows.

quiz.question: How does product-as-a-service change manufacturer incentives?
options: They profit from durability instead of planned obsolescence

details.summary: Product as a service sells access to physical products through subscriptions or pay-per-use rather than ownership. Rolls-Royce sells jet engine thrust hours instead of engines. Philips sells lighting as a service rather than bulbs. Caterpillar sells earth-moving capacity instead of machines.
details.whyItMatters: PaaS aligns manufacturer and customer incentives around durability and performance rather than planned obsolescence..
takeaways: Manufacturers sell outcomes and usage rather than physical product ownership
Aligned incentives push manufacturers toward durability over obsolescence
Recurring service revenue replaces one-time equipment sales

faq.question: How does Rolls-Royce's power-by-the-hour model work?
faq.answer: Airlines pay Rolls-Royce per flight hour rather than purchasing engines outright. Rolls-Royce retains ownership and handles all maintenance. This aligns incentives because Rolls-Royce earns more when engines run reliably and efficiently..

faq.question: Why are more manufacturers moving toward product-as-a-service models?
faq.answer: Recurring revenue is valued more highly by investors than one-time sales. Customer relationships deepen through ongoing service delivery. Data from connected products enables predictive maintenance and continuous improvement. Lower upfront costs expand the addressable market for expensive equipment.
